reason: Opened the cited Gulf News article (last updated 16 June 2026, byline Nivetha Dayanand) and it states exactly: 2.1 million guests in 2025, up 22%; revenues up 20% to Dh780 million; occupancy 78%; ADR Dh305; average stay two nights; 10,700 keys across 102 hotels; all attributed to Cavendish Maxwell (Ali Siddiqui quoted). Independent confirmation: the Zawya syndication of the TradeArabia story carries identical numbers (2.1m, +22%, AED780m/$212m, +20%, 78%, AED305, 2 nights, 102 hotels, 10,700 keys) credited to Cavendish Maxwell. A Forbes Middle East profile of Khalid Jasim Al Midfa repeats "over two million across 102 hotels in 2025" and "$212.4 million" but credits SCTDA, so the attribution is slightly muddled in secondary coverage; the primary press coverage credits Cavendish Maxwell. Two caveats on precision: (1) Zawya/TradeArabia phrases the 78% occupancy and AED305 ADR as what the sector is "currently operating at", so they may be point-in-time rather than full-year 2025 averages; (2) the "no SCTDA 2025 source-market split" clause is only partly right. I found no SCTDA full-year 2025 release with a complete nationality ranking (the latest full SCTDA split is the 30 April 2025 release on 2024: Russia >270,000, India >170,000, Europe >100,000, China >60,000, Oman 6%, Saudi 5%, Egypt 4%). However, SCTDA has published at least one 2025 source-market data point: at the UAE-Russia Tourism Dialogue in Moscow (Sharjah24, 16 June 2026), Al Midfa said Russian hotel guests rose to more than 346,000 in 2025 from about 280,000 in 2024 (+24%), holding a 17% share of international hotel guests. SCTDA also reported about 130,000 Indian guests in January to July 2025 (+38%) and called India a top-five market (WAM/Sharjah24, September 2025). The claim is therefore accurate on every number but should say that no complete SCTDA 2025 split was found, rather than implying SCTDA published nothing on 2025 source markets.
corrected_claim: Cavendish Maxwell reports that Sharjah's 102 hotels (10,700 keys) welcomed 2.1 million guests in 2025 (+22%), with annual revenue up 20% to Dh780 million, 78% occupancy, ADR Dh305, and an average stay of two nights (https://gulfnews.com/business/tourism/sharjah-hotels-draw-21-million-guests-as-airport-traffic-fuels-tourism-boom-1.500576026; same figures via Zawya/TradeArabia: https://www.zawya.com/en/business/travel-and-tourism/sharjah-hotel-guests-rise-22-to-21mln-l4i0guoz). No complete SCTDA source-market split for 2025 was found; SCTDA's latest full nationality ranking covers 2024 (https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/news/sharjah-welcomed-1-6-million-hotel-guests-in-2024-reflecting-an-11-increase/). SCTDA has released partial 2025 market data: Russian guests exceeded 346,000 in 2025 (+24% from about 280,000), a 17% share of international hotel guests (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2026/06/16/kmr8), and Indian guests reached about 130,000 in January to July 2025 (+38%) (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/09/08/Sharjah-Tourism-Authority-wraps-up-successful-2025-India-Roadshow).
